ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A basketball is thrown obliquely upward from the same position, and in two of the throws the basketball strikes the vertical wall perpendicularly, as shown in the figure. Neglecting air resistance, from being thrown to hitting the wall, in which time is the basketball's time of motion in the air shorter?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: From being thrown to hitting the wall, the time the ball moves in the air in the second time is shorter.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the left side is a vertical wall, and near the same throwing point on the right side, two parabolic trajectories are drawn. The trajectory labeled 1 is above, and its point of hitting the wall is also higher than the point where the trajectory labeled 2 hits the wall; the trajectory labeled 2 is lower, and after being thrown from the same position, it hits the wall at a lower position. Then reason: the problem states that in both times the basketball strikes the vertical wall perpendicularly, so at the instant of hitting the wall the direction of velocity should be horizontal, and the vertical component of velocity is 0. For oblique projectile motion, the position where the vertical component of velocity is 0 is the highest point of the trajectory, so the two wall-hitting points are respectively the highest points of their own trajectories. Since the vertical rise height from the same throwing point to the highest point is smaller for No. 2 than for No. 1, and rising to the highest point satisfies the vertical-direction relation h = 1/2 g t^2, that is, the smaller the rise height, the shorter the time needed to reach the highest point, so the time of motion in the air in the second time is shorter.
